challenges.name: saga-compensation-quiz
challenges.title: Sagas: compensating a failed step
challenges.description: Two statements on the "buy premium course" saga at CodeDev: the order in which a failed purchase was undone, and a refund compensation that the orchestrator retried after a timeout.

questions.question:
Orchestrator log of one purchase. The entitlement service rejected the grant, and the compensations ran in the order the orchestrator's code listed them:

10:14:02.110 saga=s_7f2 step=pay              ok      wallet u_381: 1200 -> 200
10:14:02.164 saga=s_7f2 step=enroll           ok      enrollment e_9902 active
10:14:02.231 saga=s_7f2 step=grant            failed  422 plan_not_found
10:14:02.240 saga=s_7f2 compensate=refund           ok  wallet u_381: 200 -> 1200
10:14:04.903 saga=s_7f2 compensate=cancelEnrollment ok  enrollment e_9902 cancelled

progress-service 10:14:03.518 lesson_started enrollment=e_9902 lesson=1

Statement: "Running refund before cancelEnrollment left about 2.6 seconds in which learner u_381 had an active enrollment in a premium course that was no longer paid for, and the progress service accepted a lesson in that window."
questions.explanation: True. Between 10:14:02.240 (points returned) and 10:14:04.903 (enrollment cancelled) the database held an active enrollment with a refunded payment, a state the forward flow can never produce, and the progress service used it at 10:14:03.518. Compensating in reverse order (cancelEnrollment, then refund) keeps every intermediate state equal to some prefix of the forward flow: first "paid, not enrolled", then "nothing". The misconception is that the order of compensations does not matter because the end state is the same: other services read the intermediate states too, because a saga has no isolation.

False. A timeout tells the orchestrator only that it stopped waiting; the database may have committed attempt 1 a moment later. This refund also never checks the payment status, and its two UPDATEs are not even in one transaction, so attempt 2 adds the points again whenever attempt 1 got as far as the wallet update. A compensation must be idempotent: in one transaction, update only a payment that is still 'captured' (UPDATE payments SET status = 'refunded' WHERE saga_id = $1 AND status = 'captured' RETURNING amount) and credit the wallet only when that returned a row. The misconception is that an error from a call means the call had no effect.

challenges.name: saga-buy-premium-course
challenges.title: An orchestrated saga with compensation and resume
challenges.description: Buying a premium course on CodeDev touches four services: pay (reserve points or charge the card), enroll, grant (the entitlement that unlocks the lessons) and receipt (the email). Write the seven actions and the orchestrator runSaga so that a failed step is undone by compensations in reverse order, every action can be retried, and a crash at any point resumes correctly from the saga record stored in the database. key = "<userId>:<courseId>". ACTIONS: each runs in one transaction on the copy t of the tables and must be idempotent (running it again after it committed changes nothing). pay: if payments already has the sagaId, do nothing; for method "points", balance = wallets[userId] (0 when missing): if balance < price throw BusinessError("insufficient points"), else subtract the price; then set payments[sagaId] = { userId, method, amount: price, status: "captured" } (for "card" the card network is simulated by the scripted faults). enroll: an active enrollment for the key of the same saga: do nothing; active and of another saga: throw BusinessError("already enrolled"); otherwise set { sagaId, status: "active" }. grant: set entitlements[key] = { sagaId, active: true }. receipt: if receipts has an entry for the sagaId do nothing, else push { sagaId, userId, amount: price }. refund: only when payments[sagaId] exists and is "captured": mark it "refunded" and, for points, add the amount back to wallets[userId]. cancelEnrollment: only when enrollments[key] belongs to this saga and is active: set "cancelled". revokeEntitlement: only when entitlements[key] belongs to this saga and is active: set active false. Compensations never throw: nothing to undo means do nothing. runSaga(ctx, order): load the record; if there is none, an order is valid when method is "points" or "card" and price is a positive integer: save { order, status: "running", done: [], undone: [], error: null }, or for an invalid order save status "aborted" with error "invalid order" and run nothing. Every action goes through ctx.perform(action, order), at most ctx.maxAttempts calls in a row: TransientError: call again; BusinessError: stop, the reason is its message; maxAttempts transient errors: the reason is "gave up after <maxAttempts> attempts"; let a Crash (and any other error) propagate. Status "running": run pay, enroll, grant in this order, skipping steps already in done; after each success push it to done and save; on a failure set status "compensating" and error "<step>: <reason>", save, then compensate. After grant, send the receipt: on success push "receipt" to done, status "completed", error null; on failure status "receipt_pending" and error "receipt: <reason>" - the purchase is NOT compensated; save. Compensate (status "compensating" or "stuck"): for the steps in done in reverse order run refund for pay, cancelEnrollment for enroll, revokeEntitlement for grant, skipping those already in undone; push each success to undone and save; when one still fails after maxAttempts calls set status "stuck" (keep the error), save and stop; when all succeeded set status "aborted" and save. Status "receipt_pending": retry the receipt as above. "completed" and "aborted": do nothing. The runner reads { maxAttempts, wallets, enrollments?, orders, faults?, crashes?, rerun? }. faults[sagaId][action] scripts the calls of perform in order: "transient" throws TransientError before anything is written, "fail:<reason>" throws BusinessError(reason) (for a compensation it counts as transient), "ok" or no entry runs your action in a transaction. crashes "<sagaId>:<action>#<n>": the process dies right after the n-th successful run of that action commits; the runner then calls runSaga again for that order with a fresh context (memory is lost, the database is kept). With rerun, after all orders the runner calls runSaga once more per order. It prints the call log, every saga record and the tables. Do not change the types, FakeDb, the errors, the context or the runner.
hints: After a crash, the only thing your next run knows is the saga record in the database. For every place where the process can die - after an action committed but before you saved, or between two compensations - ask: what does the record say, what will runSaga do with it, and what happens if it runs that same action a second time?

Three places decide most tests. In the forward loop, save status "compensating" with the error BEFORE the first compensation runs, or a resume goes forward again. In compensate, walk done backwards and skip what is already in undone. In the actions, check the current row first (payments.has, payment status "captured", enrollment owned by this saga and active, receipt already sent) so a second run is a no-op.

A similar flow with different steps: a ticket booking reserves a seat, then charges, then emails. If charge fails, the record { done: [reserve], status: "compensating" } is saved and releaseSeat runs. If the process dies right after releaseSeat committed, the next run reads the same record, runs releaseSeat again - it finds the seat already free and does nothing - pushes it to undone and ends "aborted". If the email fails three times, the booking stands with status "email_pending" and a later run sends only the email.
